entries.name: min-div-minus-one-minus-one-v3-errored#0
entries.script: [G0] `(BigInt.MIN / -1) - 1` at tree v3 — THROWS `ArithmeticException: Too big bigint value 2^255` from the quotient's own construction: CBigInt's constructor checks bitLength > 255 only from TREE version 3 (CBigInt.scala:18).

entries.name: min-div-minus-one-minus-one-v0-accept#1
entries.script: [G0] `(BigInt.MIN / -1) - 1` at tree v0 — 2^255 - 1 at cost 60. Below v3 the constructor does not check and `divide` adds nothing (CBigInt.scala:45), so the quotient is 2^255, out of range; `subtract`'s unconditional toSignedBigIntValueExact (:41) then passes 2^255 - 1. THE SAME BODY as the v3 row, one header byte apart.

entries.name: min-div-minus-one-v3-errored#2
entries.script: [G1] `BigInt.MIN / -1` alone at tree v3 — throws, the same construction check.

entries.name: min-div-minus-one-v0-accept#3
entries.script: [G1] `BigInt.MIN / -1` alone at tree v0 — RETURNS 2^255 at cost 35, a BigInt OUTSIDE the 256-bit signed range, as the script's value. The JVM's real answer below v3: an implementation whose BigInt type is 256 bits cannot represent it, and that red is the divergence. G0 is the in-range form of the same fact.

entries.name: twin-div-minus-one-minus-one-v3-accept#4
entries.script: [G2] `(BigInt(6) / -1) - 1` at tree v3 — THE HONEST TWIN of G0: in-range values in the same shape, -7 at cost 60. It makes G0's v3 throw the RANGE check's and not the shape's.

entries.name: twin-div-minus-one-minus-one-v0-accept#5
entries.script: [G2] `(BigInt(6) / -1) - 1` at tree v0 — -7 at 60, unchanged: G0's v0 cost is the twin's, so magnitude costs nothing.

entries.name: negate-min-v3-errored#6
entries.script: [G3] `-(BigInt.MIN)` at tree v3 — throws `BigInteger out of 256 bit range`: `negate` checks UNCONDITIONALLY (CBigInt.scala:55).

entries.name: negate-min-v0-errored#7
entries.script: [G3] `-(BigInt.MIN)` at tree v0 — throws at v0 TOO, where G1 returns the same 2^255: below v3 `divide` and `negate` DIFFER.

entries.name: min-mod-minus-one-v3-errored#8
entries.script: [G4] `BigInt.MIN % -1` at tree v3 — throws `BigInteger: modulus not positive`. Not a MIN effect: BigInt `%` is BigInteger.mod by design (BigIntegerOps.scala:84-97), see G5.

entries.name: min-mod-minus-one-v0-errored#9
entries.script: [G4] `BigInt.MIN % -1` at tree v0 — the same at v0.

entries.name: small-mod-negative-v3-errored#10
entries.script: [G5] `BigInt(7) % BigInt(-2)` at tree v3 — throws `modulus not positive`: ANY negative divisor, which is what G4's throw is.

entries.name: small-mod-negative-v0-errored#11
entries.script: [G5] `BigInt(7) % BigInt(-2)` at tree v0 — the same at v0.
